record.paper_title: Open Problems in the Function Theory of the Bergman Space
record.original_question: Call an invariant subspace I of L2_a(D) maximal if every invariant subspace containing I is either I itself or the whole space L2_a(D). Must every maximal invariant subspace of L2_a(D) have codimension 1?

evidence.quote: Let us agree to say that an invariant subspace I in L2_a(D) is maximal provided every invariant subspace containing it is either I or the whole space L2_a(D).
Problem 10.1. Must every maximal invariant subspace of L2_a(D) have codimension 1?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ denote the open unit disk, and let $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ be the Bergman space, that is, the Hilbert space of analytic functions $f:\mathbb{D}\to\mathbb{C}$ satisfying
$$\|f\|^2 = \int_{\mathbb{D}} |f(z)|^2\, dA(z) < \infty,$$
where $dA$ is normalized Lebesgue area measure on $\mathbb{D}$. A closed subspace $I\subseteq L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ is called invariant if $z\cdot I\subseteq I$, i.e., $zf\in I$ whenever $f\in I$. Call an invariant subspace $I$ of $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ maximal if every invariant subspace $J$ with $I\subseteq J\subseteq L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ satisfies either $J=I$ or $J=L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$.

Question: Must every maximal invariant subspace of $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ have codimension $1$?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem has been solved affirmatively. Hedenmalm proved that every maximal invariant subspace of the Bergman space $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ has codimension 1. Aleman–Richter and later authors extended the codimension-1 property to broader settings (including Bergman spaces over planar regions), and Guo et al. generalized it to abstract Hilbert space settings.

status_evidence.title: Recent Progress and Open Problems in the Bergman Space
status_evidence.snippet: Survey reporting progress on the open problems on Bergman spaces including the maximal invariant subspace / codimension-1 question.
status_evidence.claim: The maximal invariant subspace problem has been resolved as part of the codimension-1 property results.

status_evidence.title: The Codimension-1 Property in Bergman Spaces over Planar Regions
status_evidence.snippet: Aleman–Richter type results establishing the codimension-1 property for invariant subspaces of Bergman spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Maximal invariant subspaces of the Bergman space have codimension one.
